value.account:
WHAT I CHANGED
- New orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py: ResumeScopePath, ResumeProjectionIntegrityError, audit_scope and the diagnostic builder (the twelve reasons, v1 schema, identity-only scope_path, scalar-only offending_value). It reads only the bundle and state it gets and never mutates. Retry lineage lives in call_frame_lineage.py (index_retry_lineage, next_unused_retry_frame_id, CallFrameRetryLineageError), re-exported from the integrity module. Loop bookkeeping rules are in resume_loop_progress.py, which also owns ResumeProjectionValidationError (re-exported from state_projection).
- state_projection.py: enumerate_resume_slots (candidates, call boundaries, unclaimed explicit rows, with qualified loop/call ids built from the existing runtime_step_id APIs), resolve_resume_step_id, resolve_call_boundary; CallBoundaryProjection.import_alias (filled in lowering.py). Max-iteration range checks for repeat_until are done by the auditor from the bundle IR so no new serialized projection field was added.
- CLI (commands/resume.py): audit_scope runs after schema/checksum acceptance and before observability overrides, session/process metadata, executor construction; failure exits 1 and records only status/error/updated_at. A failing session close is logged and cannot replace the diagnostic.
- executor.py: a structurally root executor (state manager is a StateManager) rechecks the checksum via resume_root_checksum.py (workflow_checksum_mismatch envelope, four reasons) and then audits, both before the prologue. Child call-frame executors skip it. StateManager.record_workflow_checksum_mismatch / record_resume_projection_integrity_failure edit the raw JSON so unknown root fields and the run tree survive.
- calls.py + call_resume_selection.py: a reached call resolves its boundary with one resolve_call_boundary call, selects the callee by the boundary's alias, checks persisted aliases, groups frames into a lineage (Workflow Lisp is recognised only via provenance.frontend_kind), rejects a completed frame whose id equals the would-be id (call_resume_state_invalid / completed_call_frame_id_collision), and runs checksum plus audit_scope for failed predecessors and then the running member after the input/write-root/checksum/bound-input validations and before any child manager or executor exists. A callee-side projection error is promoted unchanged (never call_failed). Mapping-order frame selection was removed from frame_id_with_overrides.
- Sticky behaviour: WorkflowExecutor._execute_call records the diagnostic; _handle_control_flow returns _stop for it ahead of goto routes and on_error=continue and sets the run error; loops stop (repeat_until frame carries the unwrapped error, for_each does not start another iteration); FinalizationController keeps finalization failures supplemental (failure.error is the projection error or null) and lets a finalization-only projection error become the run error.
- Observability: forensic_state.has_forensic_current_step; build_status_snapshot shows that step as pending (no current_visit_count, not counted running), markdown no longer says in progress, and the monitor classifier ignores it as a live heartbeat.
- Also in the tree: the loader duplicate-alias / duplicate-imports check (import_alias_checks.py, hooked in loader before bundle construction) and provenance.frontend_kind == "workflow_lisp" for every compiled bundle (set in lowering/core.py, kept by build_frontend_bundle). Both were done by helper agents and I reviewed their reported results rather than line by line.
- Docs: new section in specs/state.md and acceptance entries 201-209 in specs/acceptance/index.md.
- Tests: new tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py (55 tests), tests/test_loader_import_aliases.py, tests/test_workflow_lisp_frontend_kind_provenance.py. Existing tests that encoded the old gap were rewritten to the new contract (CLI/direct-executor ordering, stale caller id, callee-local corruption, malformed call_frames, current_step mismatch) or given valid fixtures (current_step.step_id added; lexical-restore helpers no longer leave terminal repeat_until bookkeeping without its loop frame; one adjudication test skips the root recheck because it edits the workflow on purpose). Two characterization goldens gained import_alias.

VERIFICATION
- Full suite (pytest -n 16): 4736 passed, 48 failed. 47 of those fail identically on the untouched HEAD (I compared by stashing); the 48th (test_deadline_expiring_during_promotion...) passes on three reruns, so it is timing flake. pytest --collect-only on the new modules works. A real CLI run/resume smoke (failing gate, resume to completion, then a corrupted step id) behaved as specified: exit 1, reason unknown_explicit_step_id, state otherwise untouched. A repeat_until-contained call with a stale callee id produced the unwrapped diagnostic as the loop frame error and run error and did not start ProcessItems.

ALTERNATIVES / DECISIONS
- Recursing audit_scope into child frame states at the root audit: rejected, because callee checksum validation must precede callee audit and reached-callee failures must land on the caller step; each scope is audited when reached.
- Putting max_iterations on the projection: tried, dropped (it changes serialized projection goldens beyond the one field the spec names); the auditor reads it from the IR instead.
- Keeping the mapping-order resume lookup for non-Lisp frames: dropped; non-Lisp boundaries take their single non-completed frame via the lineage index.
- Provenance side effect: direct compile_stage3_entrypoint bundles with no recorded lowering schema would have failed closed in default resume; _lowering_schema_version now falls back to 1 for frontend_kind == workflow_lisp (the compiler's own default) so they keep step-granular resume.

JUDGEMENT CALLS THE SPEC LEAVES OPEN
- Reason precedence for step rows: an explicit row whose name the scope does not own is unclaimed_explicit_step_row even if its id is also unknown; unknown_explicit_step_id only applies to owned names.
- Retry lineage: the ordinal set of same-base members must be contiguous from 0, and a running member must be the newest non-completed one; otherwise it fails closed. Completed frames with other bases are history.
- A loaded object without a WorkflowStateProjection (mock loaders in old tests) skips the audit instead of failing.
- expected_owner.workflow_file is str(bundle provenance workflow_path); the checksum envelope's workflow_file is the workspace-relative display path or null.
- Reached-call frame-shape errors keep the old call_resume_state_invalid results (the root audit normally catches them first with unsupported_shape).

NOT COVERED
- No git commit was made. docs/index.md, capability matrix and design docs were not touched. The legacy (non-typed) for_each nested-step path only gets a coarse stop check, and nested loops-in-loops are not enumerated as candidates. No dedicated test for session-close failure replacement or for the CLI-then-executor second-audit race beyond the ordering tests. Pre-existing failures (47) were left alone.
value.summary: Checksum-compatible resume now audits every persisted identity (root, call frames, retry lineage, loop progress) against the current projection before any mutation or effect, fails closed with one sticky diagnostic, and ships with the YAML import-alias check, typed Workflow Lisp provenance, specs and tests.
